target.title: fix(infra): swallow mid-stream read errors in session-cost readJsonlRecords
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readJsonlRecords` in `src/infra/session-cost-usage.ts` reads session transcript files with `for await...of` over a `readline` interface backed by `fs.createReadStream`. If the underlying stream emits an error mid-read (e.g. EISDIR, EIO, or the file is truncated underneath us), the unhandled error rejects the async iterator and crashes the caller. This can happen when the usage-cost cache scans session files while another process is cleaning up or replacing them.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wrap the `for await...of` loop in a `try/catch` so mid-stream read errors are swallowed and the iterator terminates cleanly, returning the records already read. This matches the existing behavior for missing/empty transcript files and keeps `loadSessionLogs`, `scanTranscriptFile`, `loadSessionCostSummary`, and `loadSessionUsageTimeSeries` stable when a stream fails.

## User Impact

Session cost/usage views and `openclaw session logs` are less likely to surface a raw stream error when transcript files are concurrently modified or become unreadable.

## Evidence

- Regression test: `src/infra/session-cost-usage.stream-errors.test.ts` mocks `fs.createReadStream` to emit an error mid-read and asserts `loadSessionLogs` returns `[]` instead of throwing.
- Real behavior proof: `scripts/proof/session-cost-usage-readline-errors.mts` creates a directory named `proof-session.jsonl` so `createReadStream` emits `EISDIR`, then verifies `loadSessionLogs` returns an empty array.
- Local verification:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/session-cost-usage.stream-errors.test.ts` passes.
  - `node_modules/.bin/tsx scripts/proof/session-cost-usage-readline-errors.mts` passes.
  - `OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1 node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/infra/session-cost-usage.ts src/infra/session-cost-usage.stream-errors.test.ts scripts/proof/session-cost-usage-readline-errors.mts` passes.
